Visit note | 2025-11-04 04:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Lipi Hossain, 67, female. Mrs. Hossain returns for review, reporting that she continues to experience night pain in her shoulder, and she remains unable to raise her arm or reach behind her back. Her symptoms began gradually after a long illness in Bogura. She works as a retired civil servant. She denies neck pain or hand numbness, and there is no history of trauma. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Mr. Shikder attends for a follow-up consultation, complaining of an irregular fast heartbeat accompanied by dizzy spells. Visit note | 2025-11-05 10:00 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Mahfuz Bhuiyan, 61, male. Mr. Bhuiyan presents for review reporting bothersome numbness in his toes along with a persistent tingling sensation like pins and needles. He notes that these symptoms started after years of high sugar readings were found at a health camp in Khilgaon. He works as a graphic designer and lives with his family in Dhaka. He mentions that the discomfort is more noticeable at night and when wearing closed shoes. He reports no history of foot ulcers or unhealed injuries, and denies any significant weakness in his legs or difficulty with balance. On examination, neurological assessment reveals reduced sensation at 6 of 10 monofilament test sites across both feet, while ankle reflexes are diminished symmetrically. Other vitals: BP 132/76 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, weight 58 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and upper limb examination is normal. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: a prescription was issued to help manage the neuropathic discomfort. He was advised to check his feet daily for cuts and abrasions, wear soft closed shoes to prevent friction, and keep his blood sugar strictly under control. Follow-up in 6 weeks.
